overview: The Medford School Committee approved funding for an elementary school mural, student library card integration, an April 2017 high school trip to Italy, and updated district drug and alcohol policies. The committee also received reports on a high school bomb scare response, science fair accomplishments, financial updates, and legal counsel regarding facility rental policies.

items.title: Approval of Minutes, Bills, and Payrolls
items.summary: The committee approved the meeting minutes of March 28, 2016, along with bills, transfer of funds, and payrolls.

items.title: Roberts Elementary School Art Mural Funding Request
items.summary: Parent Cheryl Rodriguez presented a request for art supplies for a student mosaic mural at Roberts Elementary School, which the committee approved for up to $800 from public art funds.

items.title: Public Participation on Superintendent Succession Plan
items.summary: Resident Angela Moore recommended that the committee establish a transparent search and succession plan prior to the expiration of Superintendent Belson's contract in June 2017.

items.title: Medford High School Bomb Threat Response Report
items.summary: Superintendent Belson and Headmaster John Perella detailed the response, security protocols, building sweep, and parent communications following an automated bomb threat received at Medford High School.

items.title: Medford Public Library Youth Services Partnership
items.summary: Youth Services Librarian Sam Sednek presented digital learning resources and proposed issuing library cards to all Medford students, which the committee voted to include in new student registration packets.

items.title: Donation of Medford High School Pool Records Board
items.summary: The committee accepted the donation of a swimming records board for the high school pool from the Feeley family.

items.title: Medford High School Student Trip to Italy
items.summary: Foreign Language Director Rita DiCarlo presented a proposal for an April 2017 high school student trip to Italy, which received committee approval.

items.title: Regional Science and Engineering Fair Recognition
items.summary: Science Coordinator Rocco Cieri highlighted regional science fair awards, recognizing student Ann Lee for advancing to the Intel International Science and Engineering Fair.

items.title: Gender Identity Non-Discrimination Policy Update
items.summary: Superintendent Belson presented an update on the gender non-discrimination policy, and the committee voted to express support for pending state legislation regarding transgender public facility access.

items.title: MPS Drug and Alcohol Policy Reaffirmation
items.summary: The committee approved updates to the district drug and alcohol policy to reflect new state legislation, granting administrative discretion on social probation graduation attendance and requiring sign-offs from all staff and coaches.

items.title: District Financial Report
items.summary: Director of Finance Patricia Velie presented the financial update covering food service account balances, substitute management software, high school telephone integration, and winter utility savings.

items.title: MHS Italian Contest First Place Recognition
items.summary: Rita DiCarlo reported that ten MHS students won first place in an Italian language competition at Northeastern University, prompting a committee vote to invite the students for formal recognition.

items.title: School Rental Policy and Batting Cages Access
items.summary: Legal Counsel Howard Greenspan reviewed statutory standards and local rental policies, after which the committee referred the rental policy review to subcommittee while approving temporary batting cage access for local youth baseball and softball leagues.

items.title: Legislative Update on Charter School Cap
items.summary: The committee discussed pending state Senate charter school legislation and agreed to review a updated draft resolution letter at an upcoming Committee of the Whole meeting.

items.title: Condolence Resolutions
items.summary: The committee observed a moment of silence for former MHS history teacher Carol Caroni Mastromaro, former MHS secretary Marjorie Bennett, and former secretary Linda Houston.

items.title: Superintendent's Report and Executive Session
items.summary: Following brief administrative remarks from Superintendent Belson, the committee voted to enter executive session to discuss legal matters and collective bargaining negotiations.
